requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
I judged the reviewed tests adequate for `requirements.authoring.invocation`. I did not read implementation source. Each obligation maps to the tests below.

- **Subject selection (requirement and example).** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs `author` for a requirement and for a named example. It asserts that each report names the subject and that the written evidence has the matching `requirement` or `example` field.
- **Rejection of an absent subject.** `author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets` runs `author requirements.absent`. It asserts failure, that stderr names the subject, and that existing evidence is untouched.
- **Command form.**
  - `author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets` checks that a named subject with `--all` and `--all` with `--stdout` are rejected with exit code 2.
  - `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` (`tests/authoring_batch.rs`) covers `--missing`, `--force` and `--stdout`. It checks that `--missing` with `--force` is rejected, that `--stdout --missing` is rejected, and that `--stdout` implies `--force`.
  - `an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile` covers `--config <name>` by asserting that the alternate profile's model and key are used.
  - `verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` covers `-v` and `--verbose`.
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` covers `--stdout` with and without verbose.
- **Project resolution.** `authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file` runs from a nested directory inside the project and succeeds.
- **Completion report.**
  - `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` asserts that stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`. It also asserts an `Evidence:` line whose path resolves to `evidence/SUBJECT.json` and a `Usage:` line.
  - `initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template` asserts the same header, the evidence path, and that the usage path is an existing file.
- **Stdout mode.**
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` parses all of stdout as a single JSON record that ends with a newline. It asserts that stderr contains the `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL` header, `Evidence: stdout`, and a `Usage:` path to an existing file. It also asserts that project evidence is unchanged or not created.
  - `missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence` asserts that stdout is empty on failure in both file and `--stdout` modes. This covers diagnostics not going to stdout.
- **`author-evidence` alias.** This is used in `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` and `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files`. It is also used in `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` for a skip-as-current case and in the failed-submission test. The alias is also rejected with `--all`.
- **Cited requirements.** `requirements.authoring.refresh` behavior (keep current, force, stdout implies force) is covered in the batch test. The subsequent-assessment rules under `requirements.authoring.reassessment` are governed by that requirement and its own tests, so I did not reassess them here.

I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST initially assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current on initial selection.
After that selection, {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment` governs each round. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
:::{req} reassessment
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.
A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
